statement.antecedent: thetaBounded(theta) [0296, in-tree def]: forall eps > 0, exists C, T0 > 0, forall T >= T0, forall N (integer) in [2, T^theta]: I_N(0,T) <= C * T^(1+eps), where I_N(0,T) = int_0^T |M_N(1/2+it)|^2 |zeta(1/2+it)|^2 dt and M_N = the Levinson mollifier (0290, in-tree thetaMoll).
statement.decomposition: FIX epsilon > 0, delta := epsilon/3. Range split [2, T^theta] = [2, T^delta] v [T^delta, T^theta]. PART A (N <= T^delta): |M_N(1/2+it)| <= 2 * sum_{n<=N} n^(-1/2) <= C sqrt(N) (each mollifier weight 1 - log n/log N <= 2 for 2 <= n <= N); the classical HARDY-LITTLEWOOD pointwise second moment int_0^T |zeta(1/2+it)|^2 dt = T*log(T/2pi) + O(T) (explicit, classical - CITED, not in-tree) gives I_N(0,T) <= C1 * N * T * log T <= C2 * T^(1+delta+o(1)) = O_eps(T^(1+eps)) for N <= T^(epsilon/3). PART B (N in [T^delta, T^theta], theta' := log N/log T in [delta, theta]): the (1.2) asymptotic I_{T^theta'}(0,T)/T = 1 + 1/theta' (published 0 < theta' < 4/7; the 0293-0295 unified wall = the gap {theta | 4/7 < theta}) with the standard compact-uniform reading on [delta, theta] gives I_N(0,T) <= T * (1 + 1/delta) * (1 + o_eps(T)) = O_eps(T) = O_eps(T^(1+eps)). PARTS A + B cover the whole range [2, T^theta] with a single C_eps (max of the two bounds) and one T0 - EXACTLY the antecedent's shape.
consequences: door 2 at theta <= door 1 on [delta, theta] + the classical pointwise second moment: the 'uniform range shape' of the antecedent (0296's 'genuinely stronger shape' note) ADDS NO NEW ANALYTIC CONTENT beyond the (1.2) family + classical estimates

UPGRADE of 0296's conservative note: door 2's PUBLISHED REACH is theta <= 4/7 (cited content: (1.2)@[delta, 4/7] + Hardy-Littlewood pointwise second moment), NOT 'theta <= 1/2 pointwise shape' - the 1/2 was the Radziwill-Prop-B reading of the (1.2) proof range, not the antecedent's reach
the two doors' GAPS coincide: door 1 gap = door 2 gap = {theta | 4/7 < theta} (the 0295 unified gap) - the two doors are the SAME WALL in two shapes (sharp asymptotic shape vs big-O shape)

practical consequence for the program: attacking EITHER door past 4/7 attacks the same object; the (1.2) asymptotic (door 1) is the canonical form (it yields door 2 by the decomposition above, not conversely - the big-O shape carries no asymptotic information)
